title: Billing, budgets and cost management
learningObjective: Use the Billing console, pricing information, AWS Budgets, Cost Explorer, the Pricing Calculator, Organizations consolidated billing and cost allocation tags with the Cost and Usage Report.
foundation: The Billing and Cost Management console shows your bills and payments.
AWS Budgets alerts you when cost or usage passes a limit; Cost Explorer shows where money goes and forecasts spend; the Pricing Calculator estimates costs before you build.
AWS Organizations puts many accounts on one bill (consolidated billing), and cost allocation tags let you split costs by project or team.
engineer: Billing support: billing console, invoices, payment methods, Billing Conductor (custom billing groups), AWS Support for billing questions (available on all plans including Basic).
Pricing information: service pricing pages, AWS Price List API, Pricing Calculator (estimates, exportable, shareable).

AWS Budgets: cost, usage, RI/Savings Plans utilisation and coverage budgets; alerts on actual or forecasted values via email/SNS; budget actions can apply IAM or SCP policies or stop instances. Cost Explorer: visualise up to the past 13 months (longer with settings), forecast, rightsizing and Savings Plans recommendations.

Organizations: management account pays; consolidated billing combines usage for volume pricing tiers and shares RI/Savings Plans discounts; no extra cost. Cost allocation tags: AWS-generated (for example aws:createdBy) and user-defined tags must be activated in the billing console; they appear in Cost Explorer and the AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR / CUR 2.0 via Data Exports), the most detailed billing data delivered to S3.

animation.caption: Open 'Billing and cost tools' and 'Consolidated billing and RIs'.

example.title: FinOps basics
body: The company estimates a new project with the Pricing Calculator, tags all resources with project=atlas, activates the tag for cost allocation, sets a budget alert at 80% of forecast, and loads the CUR into Athena for monthly chargeback across 30 accounts on one consolidated bill.

prerequisites: An AWS account (use an IAM Identity Center user, not root)
permissions: Read-only access to explore; least-privilege permissions to change resources
limits: Conceptual objective: explore in the console; no configuration limits are tested
portal: Billing and Cost Management > Budgets > Create budget.
configuration.cli:
aws budgets create-budget --account-id <id> --budget file://budget.json --notifications-with-subscribers file://notify.json
aws ce get-cost-and-usage --time-period Start=2026-10-01,End=2026-11-01 --granularity MONTHLY --metrics UnblendedCost --group-by Type=TAG,Key=project
aws organizations list-accounts

lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: Tags not activated as cost allocation tags (or applied after the usage).
troubleshooting.fix: Activate them in Billing; they apply going forward.

comparisons.difference: Budgets, cost analysis, pricing calculator and exports are equivalent.

misconceptions.reality: They alert; budget actions must be configured to act.

architectureDecisions: Tag consistently, activate tags, and review Cost Explorer monthly.

walkthrough.subtitle: Run the bills for a company with many AWS accounts: one bill, tagged costs, forecasts, alerts and estimates.
learn: Cost allocation tags and the Cost and Usage Report
AWS Pricing Calculator, pricing information and billing support

steps.label: Who spent it?
steps.title: "Why is the bill 40% higher?"
body: The company has many AWS accounts. Finance gets several bills, can't tell which team spent what, and only finds out about overspending at the end of the month.

steps.label: Consolidated
steps.title: One bill with AWS Organizations
body: Put all accounts in AWS Organizations. Consolidated billing gives one bill paid by the management account, still broken down per account.
Usage is combined, so volume pricing tiers and shared RI and Savings Plans discounts benefit everyone.

steps.label: Tags
steps.title: Tag resources by team and project
body: Cost allocation tags are key-value labels on resources. AWS-generated tags (such as aws:createdBy) and user-defined tags (such as team=checkout) appear in billing only after you activate them in the Billing console.
The Cost and Usage Report (delivered through Data Exports) gives the most detailed line-item data, including tags.

steps.label: Cost Explorer
steps.title: See trends with Cost Explorer
body: AWS Cost Explorer shows costs over time, grouped by service, account, Region or tag, and forecasts future spend. Here it shows the jump came from the Data account's new cluster.

steps.label: Budgets
steps.title: Get warned with AWS Budgets
body: AWS Budgets sets a cost or usage limit and sends alerts, by email or SNS, when actual or forecast spend crosses a threshold. It can also track RI and Savings Plans coverage, and run actions such as applying a restrictive policy.

callout.text: Cost Explorer = analyse past and forecast. Budgets = alert when a threshold is crossed. Pricing Calculator = estimate before you build.

steps.label: Estimate
steps.title: Estimate before building
body: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates the monthly cost of an architecture you haven't built yet. Each service's pricing page and the AWS Price List API give the official prices.
Billing and account questions can go to AWS Support on every plan, including Basic, at no extra cost.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: See it, split it, limit it, plan it
recap: Organizations: one consolidated bill, shared discounts
Activate cost allocation tags; detailed data in the Cost and Usage Report
Pricing Calculator for estimates; billing support on all plans
